config_basis: sample restriction — households observed with and without a co-resident grandparent
arrangement_measure: presence of grandparent(s) in the household
evidence: the presence of grandparent(s) in a household has a positive impact on the number of children born (particularly when both grandparents are present), with estimates ranging from 0.0771 (95% CI: 0.0175 to 0.1368) for both grandparents to 0.1373 (95% CI: 0.0824 to 0.1922) overall
note: Fixed effects remove time-invariant household unobservables. They do NOT address the anticipation problem in scope §3: a household that expects a birth may take a grandparent in. The paper runs a lead model for reverse causation, which is the right instinct and is not an exclusion restriction.

venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
setting: Mosuo and neighbouring populations, SW China (matrilineal)
arrangement_measure: post-marital residence: own parents / husband's parents / both / neither
estimate: HR 1.306 (own parents only vs husband's parents only); HR 1.746 (both sets)
evidence: women who resided with their own parents only had earlier AFB than those living with only their husband's parents (HR = 1.306), while those living with both sets of parents had still earlier births (HR = 1.746)
note: THE DIRECTION OF THE CONTRAST IS WITHIN THE EXTENDED CELL, not extended versus independent. It says whose parents matter, which is Amendment 2's point, and it cannot be read as an effect of co-residence itself.

config_basis: sample restriction — married women co-residing with husband's parents
anticipation_control: co-residence and labour supply treated as ENDOGENOUS; full-information maximum likelihood duration model with endogenous binary variables
estimate: sign not quantified — full text paywalled
evidence: Results controlling for endogeneity suggest that both coresidence and working are associated with a delay in childbearing, reversing the effect of coresidence on the timing of first birth but not that of working.
note: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ROW IN THIS TABLE AND ITS NUMBER IS NOT IN IT. Correcting for endogeneity REVERSES the sign. Duke University Press paywalls the full text (stage 5f), so the point estimate is unavailable and the direction comes from the abstract. It is the empirical basis for Ruling 4's estimator stratum.

config_basis: none — the unit is a society, not a household
arrangement_measure: prevalence of extended family structures in the society
source_of_variation: historical crop suitability -> ancestral plough adoption, as an instrument
estimate: +1.07 children per woman per SD of extended-family prevalence
evidence: A one standard-deviation increase in prevalence of extended families is associated with approximately 1.07 additional children per woman.
note: EXCLUDED FROM EVERY POOL, AND THE REASON IS THE SCOPE'S OWN WALL 3. The unit of observation is a society and the variation is cross-cultural, which is what Wall 3 rules out: societies with and without ancestral plough agriculture differ on everything the plough literature itself documents -- female labour force participation, gender norms, inheritance. The exclusion restriction requires plough adoption to affect fertility ONLY through family structure, and the adjacent literature is largely about the other channels. The magnitude, more than a full child per standard deviation, is on its own a reason to distrust it. Recorded rather than dropped, because a reader who finds it will want to know why it is not used.

venue: Int. J. Geography, Geology and Environment
config_basis: sample split, nuclear versus extended households
estimate: 4.96 extended vs 4.65 nuclear; difference not significant
evidence: Nuclear and extended family households showed no significant difference in mean number of children (4.65 versus 4.96, p>0.2).
note: A NULL, and the only high-fertility-setting estimate in the cell. Small sample; the confidence interval is wide enough to contain the Vietnamese point estimate several times over.

config_basis: co-residence and proximity measured separately in linked census data
n: 3,173,297 couples linked; 2,047,694 in the net-reproduction models
arrangement_measure: kin co-resident in household, and surname-kin density nearby
estimate: co-resident mother IRR 0.951***; co-resident mother-in-law IRR 1.030***; nearby mother-in-law IRR 1.016***; adult surname-kin density IRR 1.283***
direction: mixed — sign depends on WHICH kin
evidence: Mother coresident in household 0.951 *** ... Mother-in-law coresident in household 1.030 *** ... Nearby mother-in-law 1.016 *** ... Adult surname kin density 1.283 ***
note: THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE IN THE CHAPTER THAT THE EXPOSURE IS NOT ONE VARIABLE. In the same 3.1-million-couple dataset, a co-resident MOTHER lowers fertility 4.9% and a co-resident MOTHER-IN-LAW raises it 3.0%. Any estimate that averages 'living with a parent' averages across that. It is also the chapter's only FDT-era evidence, and the kin-density coefficient dwarfs both co-residence terms.

venue: Vienna Institute of Demography Working Papers 03/2023
estimate: association with desire for a second child; no association with third-child desire
evidence: Multivariate regressions reveal an association between coresiding with parents and the desire for a second child, regardless of the sex of the first child. Among women with two children, third-child desires do not appear to be associated with coresiding with parents.
note: Intentions. Pools only with intentions, per Ruling 4 stratum 2.

venue: IZA DP 6651; B.E. Journal of Economic Analysis & Policy
source_of_variation: difference-in-differences and regression discontinuity at the eligibility age threshold (22)
anticipation_control: policy discontinuity at an age cutoff
tempo_or_quantum: tempo (probability of at least one child, young ages)
estimate: emancipation +0.9 to +2.3 pp; couple cohabitation +1.2 to +2.4 pp; probability of having children +4.8 to +8.1 pp (13-22% of the sample mean); no effect on marriage
evidence: Difference-in-Differences and Regression Discontinuity estimates show that the policy increases emancipation rates by 0.9-2.3 percentage points, couple cohabitation by 1.2-2.4 percentage points, and the probability of having children by 4.8-8.1 percentage points for 22 year-olds compared to 21 year-olds.
note: THE CHAPTER'S BEST DESIGN AND IT HAS A SPECIFIC, SERIOUS FLAW: the fertility effect is estimated CONDITIONAL ON BEING EMANCIPATED, and emancipation is itself moved by the treatment. Conditioning on a post-treatment variable, in a design whose whole point is that the treatment causes emancipation. The unconditional fertility effect is the estimand the chapter wants, and it is not the one reported.

config_basis: young adults; not a co-residence measure
setting: United States, state lotteries, universe of tax data 2000-2019
arrangement_measure: homeownership and household formation (not co-residence directly)
source_of_variation: lottery win, with future winners as an additional control group (triple difference)
anticipation_control: randomised windfall; placebo pre-trends indistinguishable from zero
tempo_or_quantum: BOTH, and that is the finding
estimate: homeownership +5.59 pp per $100,000 at one year; total births at five years approximately zero, ruling out an increase above 0.01 children per $100,000
evidence: One year after the lottery win, the effect of $100,000 is estimated to be 5.59 percentage points in the full sample ... Five years after the lottery win, the effect on total births is close to zero, and we can rule out an increase in the number of children of 0.01 per $100,000.
note: NOT A CO-RESIDENCE ESTIMATE, AND IT BOUNDS THE CHAPTER ANYWAY. The exposure is an unconditional cash windfall, so it belongs to the income hypothesis. What it establishes is that pure liquidity moves the TIMING of births and not their number -- which is exactly the reading scope section 7 says the A.23 verdict turns on, arriving from the cleanest identification in the packet.

venue: ECB WP 1910; Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
source_of_variation: regional house-price variation, instrumented by predetermined local industrial structure
tempo_or_quantum: not separable from what was recovered
estimate: direction only — in high price-growth MSAs the youngest households were substantially less likely to buy property, be married, or have a child, in 2006 and 2011
evidence: We find that in MSAs which experienced large increases in house prices between 2001 and 2006, the youngest households were substantially less likely to purchase residential property, to be married, and to have a child, both in 2006 and in 2011.
note: THE ONLY DESIGN IN THE FRAME THAT ESTIMATES HOUSEHOLD FORMATION AND FERTILITY UNDER ONE INSTRUMENT, which is what a decomposition of the non-additivity would need. Wiley paywalls the article and the ECB working paper was not retrieved, so the coefficients are not in hand. This is the single highest-value item on the library worklist.

evidence: We also found no evidence of significant effects on divorce, cohabitation, and fertility.
note: A NULL FROM AN IDENTIFIED DESIGN, on a policy that does move living arrangements. One of the six designs Amendment 4 adds to scope section 4.

venue: The Journal of the Economics of Ageing
config_basis: pension eligibility of the ELDERLY parent
setting: rural China, New Rural Pension Scheme
source_of_variation: fuzzy regression discontinuity at the pension eligibility age
estimate: adult sons co-residing with parents -0.389*** (Guizhou); grandchildren co-residing with grandparents -0.137*** (Guizhou); Shandong estimates insignificant
evidence: Sample of adult sons Co-residing with parent(s) (Guizhou) 1016 -.389***(.081) ... Sample of the grandchildren from the sons' families Co-residing with grandparent(s) (Guizhou) 682 -.137***(.051)
note: THE HOMONYM SITTING ON THE WALL, exactly as scope section 6 predicted. The exposure is a pension to the ELDERLY parent, which is the elder-support reading; the measured outcome includes GRANDCHILDREN co-residing with grandparents, which is the extended-couple reading. Same household, same dataset, two configurations. It is link 1 either way, since no fertility outcome is estimated, and it is the strongest available evidence that the arrangement responds to something exogenous.

venue: Review of Economics of the Household
source_of_variation: district variation in court inefficiency interacted with the reform
evidence: household formation intentions = CourtIneff*Post = 0.0383*; fertility intentions = CourtIneff*Post = 0.0406**
note: Intentions on both sides of the link, and the two coefficients are almost identical -- which is what the chapter would predict if the arrangement and the birth are governed by the same expectation rather than one causing the other.

source_of_variation: cross-metro variation in affordability; Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition with a Heckman selection correction
anticipation_control: selection model, not an exogenous shock
estimate: up to a quarter of the 9-percentage-point rise in the co-residence share 2000-2021 attributed to declining affordability
evidence: attribute up to a quarter of the observed 9-percentage-point increase in the co-residence share between 2000 and 2021 to a decrease in housing affordability
note: THE EXPOSURE TREND'S BEST MAGNITUDE, and the input the demographic-significance section needs for the C.2.c-to-A.23 share. Not a fertility estimate.

config_basis: life-course transitions of women, Spanish Fertility Survey 2018
arrangement_measure: leaving the parental home (event and timing)
estimate: association reported, no transportable magnitude extracted
direction: positive (leaving home associated with higher probability of motherhood)
evidence: Leaving the parental home also shows a strong association with the likelihood of motherhood, although it also appears to be mediated by the woman's economic, union, and employment status.
note: THE AUTHORS STATE THE CHAPTER'S THREAT 1 THEMSELVES: 'it may be assumed that the desire to become a mother favours leaving home and co-residential union.' The association is real and it is not evidence about a direction. Included so the pre-launch cell is characterised rather than reported as empty.

config_basis: none — the unit is a municipality
arrangement_measure: household structure composition of the municipality
evidence: la configuracion y la consolidacion de cierto tipo de hogares son capaces de explicar el comportamiento de la fecundidad o, en sentido contrario, los niveles de fecundidad pueden constituir un factor determinante para una tipologia especifica de hogar, esto implica ... un problema de la causalidad
note: ECOLOGICAL, and the paper says in its own framing that the causal direction is a problem. Municipality-level household composition against municipality-level fertility. Recorded, not pooled.
